newsitem.title: UK: Big North Sea premiums hold as October sells out.
newsitem.headline: Big North Sea premiums hold as October sells out.

text.p: North Sea physical grades maintained strong premiums on Wednesday as dealers started to concentrate on early November cargoes ahead of next week's loading programme releases.
Outside Brent and cross-month cargoes dealers said just one Oseberg remained available for October leaving premiums at about +50 cents for the Norwegian grade and +45 cents for Forties.

"There are no signs of weakness just yet. October's all but sold out," said a trader. "Signs are that term buyers will want their November cargoes at the start of the month to take advantage of refining margins," said another.
But dealers said an even narrower Brent/WTI arbitrage on Wednesday, in 10 cents to under 90 cents, might put pressure on differentials further aheadd.
Dated Brent held steady value on Wednesday in a sale at Nov plus 10 cents.
Two Brent cargoes loading Oct 24-26 both were kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline, one by equity holder Murphy.
Nigerian spot crude differentials took off as dealers competed to grab cargoes of the West African producer's gas oil-rich grades for November loading.
"The market is really taking off, but everything's being kept under wraps," said one trader.
Dealers said cargoes of Forcados had traded at a 20 cent premium over official selling prices, due for release next week.
They said Dated Brent related differentials for Forcados were difficult to pin down with trades kept private ahead of Nigerian National Petroleum Corp's pricing announcement.
But Forcados buyers had appeared in the low 70 cent premiums over Brent, they said.
